text:
[RARC.5.4.9] **The order key is unique, and a duplicate is a defect in
the runtime.** [RARC.5.4.7]'s comparator is a **total** order only while the
pair (ordinal, creation timetag) is unique. Under [LDET.5.5]'s timetag it is:
no rule holds two activations with one timetag after any history, so a correct
runtime never meets a duplicate. A runtime may check for one, and on finding it
must treat it as an unrecoverable fault and halt the tier ([LERR.1.4.7]),
because the agenda then has no defined next activation and the firing order
[LDET.5] commits to is not determined by the artefact.

**The engine must not break the tie by any other means.** A
tiebreak the comparator does not specify is a hash-order
dependence under another name, which [RARC.5.4.8] forbids —
and it would be worse than the fault it conceals, because the
run would complete and its output would look ordinary while
being unreproducible on any other implementation.

idris.name: rarc_5_4_9__keys_distinct
idris.note: NO TWO ACTIVATIONS OF ONE RULE SHARE A TIMETAG: distinct live matches have distinct keys, since over distinct working memory a key determines its match -- the uniqueness under [LDET.5.5]'s timetag the clause rests its total order on.

idris.name: rarc_5_4_9__unique_after_history
idris.note: After any history from a loaded network no terminal holds two activations with one timetag: 'no rule holds two activations with one timetag after any history', proved. So the duplicate the clause calls a defect in the runtime cannot occur, the check it permits a runtime to make never finds one, [RARC.5.4.7]'s comparator is total, and the tiebreak the clause forbids is never needed.
